text:
Sam: heads up — saw canary traffic jump around this morning (20% -> 3% -> 18% within ~4m). App metrics show mixed model and stale KV cache hits. Anyone else?
Maria: saw alerts too. which rollout?
Sam: /deployments/service-X/canary v3 -> v4. Config looked normal but routing logs show a lot of `fallback_to_stable` entries.
Ben: can you paste the rollout policy?
Sam: sure — here's the relevant part:```json
{
  "split": {"stable": 0.8, "canary": 0.2},
  "guards": [
    {"type":"hash_prefix","key":"session_id","buckets":100},
    {"type":"header","header":"x-edge-region","match":["eu","apac"],"route":"stable"},
    {"type":"sticky_cookie","name":"_sess_route"}
  ]
}
```
Maria: hmm the header guard is second. If header guard routes to stable it overrides the hash? I thought hash was primary.
Ben: runtime evaluates guards in order. hash_prefix returns a bucket (canary/stable) — but if sticky_cookie is below header, cookie can be ignored when header guard triggers. Looks like header guard is more aggressive for certain regions and constantly flips because some clients send `x-edge-region` inconsistently (CDN edge flapping).
Carol: also saw weirdness in sticky cookie handling: when a request was routed to canary, cookie set on path `/` but later requests from same client hit `/api/v2` and cookie path mismatch so they were re-evaluated and hit header guard -> stable. So bounce is cookie path + header precedence.
Sam: logs: `route_eval: hash=17->canary; guard[1]=header->stable; guard[2]=sticky_cookie->no_cookie -> final=stable` repeated a lot.
Ben: temporary mitigation: reorder guards so sticky_cookie is checked first, then hash, then header. That would keep affinity. But I'm worried header-based overrides were intentionally higher priority for compliance reasons.
Maria: right — header was added to force stable for certain low-latency regions during maintenance windows. We can't just drop it. But we can make header guard a "soft" guard that doesn't override existing sticky assignment.
Dan: suggestion: change header guard type to `prefer` rather than `force`; implement tie-breaker: if sticky_cookie present, honor it; otherwise apply header. Minimal code change: in route evaluator, when a guard returns `route` but there is `sticky_cookie` earlier in policy, do not override.
Ben: patch idea posted:```diff
- evaluate guards in order and accept first route
+ evaluate guards in order but track affinity sources; if a later guard would override an existing affinity from a cookie/hash, only override if guard.priority==force
```
Carol: agreed. Also fix cookie path behavior: set cookie `Path=/` for our service boundaries only in router response header (was missed by middleware for `/api/v2`).
Sam: I'll open a quick PR for the evaluator change (non-breaking) and another to normalize cookie path. Can we hotfix to staging and let it run for 30m?
ops-bot: deploy requested by Sam: branch=fix/canary-guard-priority, env=staging. CI passed, rolling to 2 instances. :rocket:
Ben: after staging run, let's add a telemetry counter for "guard_override_events" that increments when later guard overrides a prior affinity. That will help catch similar cascades.
Maria: good call. Also add a small dashboard tile in Rollouts -> Canary Insights that shows bounce rate and guard_override_events over time.
Dan: I'll own the dashboard and telemetry. Assigning follow-ups: PR#1245 (evaluator), PR#1246 (cookie path), Dash ticket #OPS-912.
Sam: thx team. If staging looks good I'll nominate for canary tomorrow morning.
Maria: :thumbsup:
Ben: note — we'll need a short postmortem blurb for product so they can explain why traffic dipped during the maintenance window. Keep it simple: header guard + cookie path + precedence bug.
Carol: adding timeline to ticket now.
Sam: closing loop here once staging green. Thanks.
